 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Pavan Kumar Saxena - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri S.K.Shrivastava - Public Prosecutor for the respondent/S
 Judgment

Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Learned counsel for the appellant at the outset submits that he does not want to press Interlocutory Application for suspension of sentence and, therefore, seeks permission to withdraw the same.
However, he insist for final hearing of this appeal.

Since learned Government Advocate has no objection to said prayer, therefore, interlocutory application for suspension of sentence is dismissed as withdrawn and with consent of learned counsel for the parties appeal is heard finally.

2. This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 20.5.2025 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act), Singrauli in S.C.No.16/2023 whereby the learned trial Court has convicted appellant (Chandrabali Jogi) under sections 363, 366, 376(3) & NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50578 2 CRA-5820-2025 376(2)(N) of IPC, so also 3/4(2), &
5(L)/6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced him as under:-

Shri Pavan Kumar Saxena, learned counsel for the appellant submits that victim is a consenting adult.

Thus, consensual sexual relationship between two consenting adults will not fall either under offence of rape as defined under section 375 of IPC or under section 3/5 of POCSO Act and,
therefore, the conviction recorded by the trial Court on the basis of surmises and conjectures without appreciating the evidence, which has come on record, especially that of the victim (PW.1)
and her parents (PW.3 & PW.4) so also the School Teacher (PW.2) and Lady Doctor Jyoti Singh (PW.6), being not in favour of the prosecution, is arbitrary and cannot be sustained.
It is also submitted by learned counsel that DNA report (Ex.P/22) is negative.
The victim (PW.1) has admitted that she was in love relationship with the appellant, established physical relationship with her consent and left her home on her own volition.
It is also submitted that on the date of incident the victim was not minor.
There is no external or internal injury on the body of the victim.
The victim was consenting party.
4. Learned Government Advocate has supported the impugned judgment and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50578 3 CRA-5820-2025 prayed for dismissal of instant appeal.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
From perusal of Ex.P/22 (DNA report) it is revealed that from underwear of the victim (Exhibit-A), vaginal slide (Exhibit-B) and pubic hair (Exhibit-C), no male DNA profile (Y-STR) is found.
Victim (PW.1) in paragraph 9 of her cross-examination has admitted that she was in love relationship with the appellant.
It is also admitted that appellant established physical relationship with her consent.
In paragraph 6 she has admitted that for 2-3 years she had failed in the school and her name in the school was recorded after much delay.
She also admitted that since her brother had scolded her, she left the home on her own volition.

6. PW.2-School Headmaster(Shriram Kushwaha) has stated that though in the school record (Ex.P/4) the date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 13.4.2008 and date of admission in school is mentioned as 22.7.2013 but he had not given admission to the victim.
He also admitted that in a rural set up of a village when children grow up then their parents admit them in school after reducing their age.
He further admitted that he has no knowledge as to on what basis the date of birth of victim is recorded in the school register.
7. PW.3 (mother of the victim) has stated that age of the victim is 19-20 years.
She does not know the date of birth of the victim.
Her deposition was recorded on 27.9.2023 whereas the incident is reported to be of 24.2.2023.
In cross-examination she admitted that current age of the victim is 20 years and she had performed marriage of the victim.

sentences.text: 8. PW.4 (father of the victim) stated that age of the victim is 19-20 years.
In cross-examination he admitted that date of birth of the victim is not known to him.
He has also admitted that he had not gone to school to admit her.
In paragraph 8 he further admitted that when victim had taken admission in Class-I at that time she was of 09 years.
This means, as per PW.2 victim had taken admission in Class-I on 22.7.2013, the year of birth of victim will be of 2004.
Thus, aforesaid evidence corroborates the story of defence that victim was a consenting adult on the date of incident.
9. PW.6 (Dr.Jyoti Singh) has stated that there was no external or internal injury on the body of the victim.
Her secondary sexual characters were fully developed.
Her U.P.T. Test was negative.
There was no mark of injury on the internal part of body of victim.
Her hymen was old torn.
Victim herself admitted to be a consenting party.
School Headmaster (PW.2) who admits that victim had not taken admission during his regime.
PW.3 (mother of the victim) admits that victim was 19-20 years at the time of incident.
PW.4 (father of victim) admits that when victim had taken admission in Class-I in year 2013 she was 09 years of age.
All these reveal that year of birth of the victim to be of 2004 and the incident is of year 2023, which shows that victim was a consenting adult on the date of incident.

10. When all these aspects are taken into consideration, the same reveal that relationship between two consenting adults will not fall under abduction or rape, especially in view of admission of victim herself.
Thus, an adult leaving her home on her own volition will not attract provisions of section 363 & 366 of IPC are not attracted.

As far as admission of victim that her relationship with appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50578 5 CRA-5820-2025 was with her consent and when it has come on record that she was a consenting adult, then provisions of section 375 IPC or that of section 3/5 of the POCSO Act will also not be attracted.

Therefore, we have no hesitation in holding that conviction of the appellant is based on surmises and conjectures and prosecution has failed to prove that victim was minor a on the date of incident so as to attract the provisions of POCSO Act.
Hence, the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence needs to be set aside.
11. In the result, appeal is allowed.
Impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court is set aside.
If the custody of the appellant is not required in any other case he be released forthwith.
12. Let original record of the trial Court be sent back to the concerned Court alongwith copy of this judgment.
(VIVEK AGARWAL ) (AVANINDRA KUMAR S  JUDGE JUDGE  RM Chandrabali Jogi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025
